name: Cyprus
overview: Cyprus is a significant island in the New Testament narrative, noted as the birthplace of Barnabas, a Levite called the son of consolation. It was an early center for gospel preaching, where scattered believers preached primarily to Jews and later to Gentiles, as seen when Barnabas and Saul visited and preached in the synagogues at Salamis and Paphos. The island also hosted key missionary journeys, including the work of Barnabas and Mark, highlighting its role in spreading the gospel amid opposition, such as encountering the false prophet Barjesus.
